g.title: Pipeline
g.text: LEG 2 driven by PoW difficulty mechanism; LEG 5 timing via hash-graph (LEG 7)
Updates from v4: parameters in LEG 2 set by PoW difficulty mechanism (adjusted based on observed network behavior);
LEG 5 timing now measured via hash-graph propagation (LEG 7), not wall-clock; H/SHAKE256 question still open;
v7 adds the target-properties panel (Colton's four requirements) mapped to legs

g.title: cluster_submitters
g.text: All participants submit through same path; protocol is hardware-agnostic

g.title: requirements
g.text: Target properties — what the output must satisfy
delivered by LEG 4 sampling + LEG 5 timing
delivered by LEG 5 XEB + LEG 6 extraction
— anyone can check with a laptop
delivered by LEG 3 determinism + LEG 7 anchoring
delivered by LEG 1 seed + LEG 5 timing window

g.title: randao_alt
g.text: Not chosen: vulnerable to last-revealer attack

g.title: leg2
g.text: {circuit family, n, d, χ, t_threshold, m, ε}
(parameters must be locked before VRF seed is revealed)
Parameters set by PoW difficulty mechanism,
adjusted based on observed network behavior (TBD)

g.title: leg5
g.text: Check: F_XEB ≥ χ AND submission received within timing window
Empirical security: classical adversaries competing and failing
provide a real-time lower bound on attack cost
Timing mechanism: hash-graph propagation via LEG 7 (TBD)

g.title: bell_alt
g.text: Not chosen: requires loophole-free Bell-test hardware,

g.title: twine
g.text: Intertwined hash chains across all parties:
VRF chain · orchestration chain · miner chains ·
adversary chain · validator chain · drand wrapper ·
public output chain · private outputs chain
Defends: post-hoc tampering, collusion across audit parties
Anchors all outputs (winning + non-winning) for re-verification
Load-bearing for LEG 5: gossip propagation provides canonical timing
